expectations.text: The critical journeys were walked and the records validate
Verification and three blind ratings exist

expectations.text: Recall of the seeded analytical defects is at least 0.6
expectations.evidence: 10 of 11 seeded defects matched by criterion and route (D01→F-0008, D02→F-0006, D03→F-0006, D04→F-0006, D05→F-0017, D06→F-0008, D07→F-0006, D08→F-0013, D09→F-0015, D10→F-0006); 41 confirmed finding(s), 36 judged

expectations.text: Precision after verification is at least 0.8
expectations.evidence: 26 of 36 confirmed judged findings are a seeded defect or a real problem (strict: 11 of 36); recall by meaning 9 of 11. Grader: Of the 36 judged (non-tool) findings, 11 map to seeded defects (F-0006 D04, F-0008 D01, F-0011 D07, F-0017 D05, F-0022 D09, F-0023 D03, F-0035 D02, F-0037 D10, F-0043 D08, F-0090 D10, F-0066 D09), 15 are real-unseeded and 10 are not-a-problem (the design-polish items F-0052, F-0053, F-0091, F-0056, F-0059, F-0094, F-0063, F-0095, F-0097 and the card-state preference F-0014), so precision = 26/36 = 0.72, below 0.8; both graders also fell short at 27/36 = 0.75. Strict precision = 11/36 = 0.31; recall by meaning = 9/11, with D06 (per-metre prices, total only on review) and D11 (confirmation lacks the gate window, VHF channel and pontoon location) never reported; the reply even praises the berth cards for putting 'size limit, tide behaviour and price side by side'.

expectations.text: Severity ratings land in the expected bands for most matched defects
expectations.evidence: by the graders' mapping: 9 of 9 found defects have a mapped finding rated within band ± 0.5 (by the script's criterion matcher: 5 of 10 rated matches within band ± 0.5)

expectations.text: Report language passes the lint and the level is not overstated
expectations.evidence: report-lint 0 violation(s); achieved none; human confirmations 0

expectations.text: The reply puts the fixes in priority order and says what needs a person
expectations.evidence: The reply opens with '## Fix first' numbered 1-7, item 1 being '"Booking stopped" is a dead end (the blocker...)', followed by '## Also worth doing before launch (quick, P2)', so the P0 and P1 items come before the P2 list. It names what needs a person: 'Three questions to settle with real skippers' (which length skippers type, UTC read as local, boats without MMSI), 'no screen-reader or real-user testing yet', 'none has been confirmed by you or by real skippers yet', and an agree/disagree sheet 'for you or the harbour office to mark up'.

expectations.text: No fixture source file was modified

grader_mapping.title: Booking stopped gives no reason, no field, no fix, loses data
grader_mapping.reason: Same dead end as D04: a length over the berth limit replaces the form with 'Booking stopped' and a bare reference BK-409, with no explanation, no route back, no suggestion of the berths that fit, and the entered values gone.

grader_mapping.title: Change dates hidden behind icon-only '...' overflow button
grader_mapping.reason: Same problem as D01: the only in-flow way to change the arrival date on the berth list is a Change dates link inside an unlabelled More options disclosure, so skippers are unlikely to recognise that the action exists.

grader_mapping.title: Berth chosen before boat length is asked; mismatch found only at the end
grader_mapping.reason: A genuine sequencing problem: the skipper must hold their LOA in mind and compare it with each card's limit, and a wrong pick is only discovered after filling the whole boat form. It is not D06 (that defect is about per-metre prices and the hidden total, which the finding never mentions) and not D04 (that defect is the content and behaviour of the stopped page; reordering the flow would not change what that page says or does).

grader_mapping.title: Boat form reset on every pageshow, including Back from review
grader_mapping.reason: Same as D07: app.js resets the boat form on pageshow, so returning from the review with Back empties every boat detail and the skipper retypes all of them.

grader_mapping.title: Invalid-state border only on inputs, not the arrival-time select or berth cards
grader_mapping.reason: A concrete inconsistency in error presentation: the select and the berth cards get aria-invalid but no on-control cue, so the control in error is harder to spot than a text input in error and the error-recovery experience differs by control type. Low severity but genuine, and not among the seeds.

grader_mapping.title: Berth cards have no card-level selected or focus state
grader_mapping.reason: The finding's own words concede that both states exist on the control: 'the selected berth is indicated only by the 24 px native radio dot and the focus ring sits on that 24 px radio, not on the card.' Its complaint is scope (CMP-01's 'at the size of the card'), not absence: a 24 px radio with a visible focus ring is a perceivable selection cue and a visible focus indicator, so neither H1 nor any WCAG criterion fails. Grader B's harm ('the card's hover border looks like a selection cue', 'a skipper can be unsure which berth is chosen') is not in the finding, which reports a stylesheet inspection ('no :has(:checked) or :focus-within rule') and no observed confusion; a hover border does not even apply on the phone walkthrough. Under MAPPING-INSTRUCTIONS that is a design preference and speculative without basis in what the review shows, so not-a-problem. This stays consistent with F-0013 (agreed real-unseeded), where the select and the radios carry no on-control error cue at all; here the cue exists but is smaller than the component standard prefers.

grader_mapping.title: Past or out-of-season arrival dates are accepted
grader_mapping.reason: Genuine: the declared min/max are ignored (novalidate, presence-only check), so a skipper who mistypes a year or picks a date before today or outside the season is shown berths as free and can make a booking that cannot be honoured, with no message. Not one of the seeded defects.

grader_mapping.title: Berth error-summary link targets a non-focusable fieldset
grader_mapping.reason: Genuine accessibility problem: following the summary link scrolls to the fieldset but keyboard and screen-reader focus does not reach a radio, so keyboard users must hunt for the control themselves. Not seeded.

grader_mapping.title: Tide table in UTC while arrival times are local
grader_mapping.reason: Same as D05: high-water times are stated in UTC while the arrival-time select and the office work in BST, so the table is an hour out for the sill gate.

grader_mapping.title: Tide table is a fixed week unrelated to the chosen date
grader_mapping.reason: Genuine and distinct from the seeds: the tide data is seven hard-coded rows for 17-23 October while dates up to 31 March 2027 are bookable, so for any other date the skipper has no tide or gate information at all. D05 is the time zone and D09 is the select accepting closed-gate times; neither is about the data being static.

grader_mapping.title: Confirmation omits the arrival time shown on review
grader_mapping.reason: Genuine: the record the skipper keeps lacks the time the office expects the boat, because app.js forwards only date, nights and berth. D11 is about missing arrival instructions (gate window, VHF channel, where the visitor pontoon is), not the booked time, so adding the time row would not fix D11.

grader_mapping.title: Booking reference built from MMDD and berth only, so it repeats
grader_mapping.reason: Shown from the code and certain to occur: the same berth on the same day of another year, or a cancel-and-rebook of the same day, yields the same reference, so the reference the skipper is told to keep cannot uniquely identify their booking when they quote it to the office. Not seeded.

grader_mapping.title: Arrival time when the sill gate is shut accepted with no feedback
grader_mapping.reason: Same as D09: 08:00 on 17 October, when the gate is shut, is accepted and carried to the berth list with no warning.

grader_mapping.title: Which boat length counts is not stated; no unit on Length
grader_mapping.reason: Same as D03: the field says only 'Length', with no unit and no statement that length overall is what the berth limits use, so a skipper with a bowsprit may enter the shorter hull length.

grader_mapping.title: Review page has no change links
grader_mapping.reason: Genuine: a check-your-answers page with no way to correct an item forces the skipper to use browser Back, which on this site wipes the boat form. Distinct from D02 (orientation and step count) and from D07 (the reset itself).

grader_mapping.title: No step indicator or progress across the booking
grader_mapping.reason: Same as D02: nothing on any of the four pages says how many steps there are or where the skipper is.

grader_mapping.title: MMSI required with no explanation and no option for boats without one
grader_mapping.reason: Same as D10: MMSI is an unexplained acronym with no hint, the error only repeats 'Enter the MMSI', and there is no way to continue without one.

grader_mapping.title: Boat page does not show the chosen berth or its size limit
grader_mapping.reason: Genuine: the page says it checks the fit against 'the space you chose' but never names the berth or its limit, so the skipper must recall it and cannot catch a mismatch before submitting into the dead end. Not seeded (D06 concerns price, D04 the stopped page).

grader_mapping.title: Back from confirmation shows an editable review page with no notice
grader_mapping.reason: Genuine: after confirming, Back returns to the review page with details filled and an active Confirm booking button and no sign the booking exists, so a skipper can confirm again and double-book. Not seeded.

grader_mapping.title: Berth, pontoon space and mooring used for the same thing
grader_mapping.reason: Same as D08: visitor berth on the start page, pontoon space on the berth list, mooring on the review page.

grader_mapping.title: Tide times link mid-booking opens an empty booking form
grader_mapping.reason: Genuine, if minor: a skipper who checks the tides from the berth list lands on the start page with an empty date and time and may believe the booking is lost and start over; only browser Back restores it. Not seeded.

grader_mapping.title: Error-summary link scrolls the select flush to the top, hiding label and message
grader_mapping.reason: Observed at 375 px: following the link focuses the select with its label 'Arrival time' and the red message above the viewport, so the user lands on an unlabelled control. Small but genuine; not seeded.

grader_mapping.title: Visible 'Book a berth' link discards date, nights and time without warning
grader_mapping.reason: Genuine silent data loss through the obvious route, and inconsistent with the hidden Change dates link that keeps the values. Related to D01 but a different problem: D01 is that the change-dates action cannot be found; this is that the visible link throws the entries away.

grader_mapping.title: MMSI accepts a malformed five-digit value
grader_mapping.reason: Genuine: a mistyped MMSI passes with no message and reaches the review, so the office receives an unusable identifier. Format validation is distinct from D10, which is about the missing explanation.

grader_mapping.title: MMSI has no hint about what it is or its format
grader_mapping.reason: Same as D10: no explanation of the abbreviation or of what to enter.

grader_mapping.title: Review omits the draught and MMSI entered
grader_mapping.reason: Genuine: both values are required and consequential (whether the boat floats in the berth, how the office reaches it) yet the last check does not show them, so a typo cannot be caught. Not seeded.

grader_mapping.title: Tide table headers misaligned with right-aligned times
grader_mapping.reason: The finding reports a desktop-only alignment offset: at 1280 'Morning sits ~80px left of its figures and Afternoon appears closer to the morning times', filed under DES-execution at severity 1.33, the same polish tier as F-0053, F-0056, F-0063, F-0091 and F-0097, which both graders mapped to not-a-problem. The table's figures are 24-hour times (the review itself quotes 'high water 02:08 and 14:32 UTC'), so the two columns are self-labelling: a header read against the neighbouring figure cannot change which high-water times the skipper takes for the day, because the row ('Sat 17 Oct') carries both and each time states its own half of the day. Grader A's 'read against the wrong column' is speculative without basis in what the review shows and would not alter the planned window; the genuine tide-table hazards are already credited to D05 (UTC) and F-0018 (fixed week). Cosmetic, so not-a-problem.

grader_mapping.title: Summary values wrap to three lines at 320 px
grader_mapping.reason: The values remain legible; wrapping and stranded words at 320 px are typographic polish, not a usability problem for skippers.

grader_mapping.title: Booking reference breaks across lines at its hyphen
grader_mapping.reason: 'BK-' / '409.' at 375 px is cosmetic; the reference still reads as one item and the finding shows no confusion.

grader_mapping.title: One-word last lines in headings and hints
grader_mapping.reason: Stranded last words are a matter of typographic taste with no effect on the task.

grader_mapping.title: Identity floor missing; generic look
grader_mapping.reason: An aesthetic judgement about branding and focal points; it names no effect on a skipper completing the booking.

grader_mapping.title: Overflow menu opens in flow and pushes the berth list down
grader_mapping.reason: A disclosure that opens in flow is an accepted pattern; whether it should overlay instead is design preference and the finding shows no harm.

grader_mapping.title: Footer stops short, leaving empty page ground below it
grader_mapping.reason: Cosmetic layout observation with no effect on skippers.

grader_mapping.title: Booking reference lacks prominence on the confirmation
grader_mapping.reason: The reference is bold and findable within the sentence; a dedicated panel is a design preference, and this is not D11 (missing arrival instructions).

grader_mapping.title: Sill-gate window has no visual form and is not connected to the arrival-time choice
grader_mapping.reason: Same underlying problem as D09: the gate rule exists only as a footnote and a stock table away from the arrival-time select, so closed-gate times are chosen unknowingly; surfacing the window at the point of choice is the D09 fix. (It also touches D11 in passing, but the time-choice disconnect is its substance.)

grader_mapping.title: Wide viewports leave the right side empty
grader_mapping.reason: A narrow content column on wide screens is a common, readable layout; this is taste.

grader_mapping.title: Compared number without tabular figures: 'Sat 17 Oct'
grader_mapping.reason: Proportional digits in one date header cell do not affect reading the tide table; a typographic nicety.

grader_mapping.title: One word on the last line: 'walls.'
grader_mapping.reason: Stranded word at 320 px is typographic taste.

grader_mapping.title: One word on the last line: 'space'
grader_mapping.reason: Heading wrap at 320 px is cosmetic.

grader_mapping.title: One word on the last line: 'float'
grader_mapping.reason: Hint wrap at 320 px is cosmetic.

grader_mapping.title: One word on the last line: '15:00'
grader_mapping.reason: The time remains visible on its own line; cosmetic wrap at 320 px.
